title: He touched the blind…
paragraphs:
He touched the blind…
but not every blind man.

He raised the dead…
but cemeteries were still full.
So what gives?
If God can heal—why doesn’t He heal everyone?
Listen close.
Because healing… is not the end of the story.

In the Gospels, Jesus heals with power that stops hearts.
Lepers cleansed. Paralytics walking. Demons fleeing.
But then something strange happens.

In John 5, there’s a pool full of sick people—a crowd.
Jesus walks in… and heals one man.
One.
And walks away.

That’s not lack of power.
That’s purpose.
Here’s what we miss.

God’s mission was never just to fix bodies.
It was to rescue souls.
Because even the healed… still die.

Lazarus walked out of the tomb in John 11—
but one day, he died again.

Temporary healing is mercy.
But eternal healing? That’s salvation.
And that’s where grace walks in.

The deeper sickness is sin.
The quieter disease is separation from God.

And Jesus didn’t come just to patch wounds—
He came to carry the cross.

At Calvary, He didn’t heal Himself.
He stayed.

Bleeding.
Bruised.
Buried.
Why?
So that one day, every tear—not just some—will be wiped away.
Does God still heal today?
Yes.

Sometimes instantly.
Sometimes through doctors.
Sometimes… not yet.
And that “not yet” hurts. I know.
Some scholars interpret suffering as part of God’s mysterious will in a fallen world, not always fully revealed this side of eternity.
But Scripture is clear on this:

God is not absent in your pain.
He is working through it.

Romans 8 says He works all things for good—
not all things feel good, but none are wasted.
So why doesn’t He heal everyone?
Because He’s doing something bigger than we can see.

A healing that doesn’t end at the grave.
A restoration that no disease can touch.

Through Jesus, the final answer isn’t “Why not now?”
It’s “Wait… and watch what I will do forever.”
If you’re still waiting for healing—don’t lose heart.

The same Jesus who sometimes says “Rise and walk”
also says, “Come to Me… and I will give you rest.”
And that rest?

It’s deeper than a cured body.
It’s a redeemed soul.

From unanswered prayers to unshakable faith—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
